prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: offshore-wind acceptance/O&M/refurbishment/decommissioning; excludes beyond-connection grid/unrelated ports. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal. Turbine Controller executes authorized bounded commands, reports state/Pitch Deviation Notice; local protection overrides remote commands. Pitch System adjusts blades; Converter Cabinet converts electricity under limits/interlocks; Nacelle Condition Monitor supplies health measurements; Rotor Brake Unit/Turbine Sensor Bus are turbine elements. Offshore Substation/Main Transformer collect/switch power; Export Cable Monitor monitors exports; Grid Interface Relay interfaces grid. SCADA Gateway provides authorized Shore Control Room status/control and requested current status to permit reviewers; deviation notices flag technical-review packages. SCADA Engineer maintains interfaces; Control Engineer reviews alarms; commands require authorization/logging; availability/function/prohibited-path checks follow changes. Vessel AIS Receiver timestamps broadcasts/produces Position Quality Flag; Marine Coordinator uses Fleet Dispatch Console/checks access; Vessel Master confirms transfers/retains safety judgment. Duty Planner produces Transfer Manifest Addendum, checks/queues requests/resolves supply/scheduling. Weather Hold needs confirmed-safe resumption. Metocean Buoy retains timestamped observations through outages; validated data feeds Weather Service/Squall Window Bulletin; Weather Analyst advises; require robust sensors/thresholds/synchronization/health-checks. Blade Specialist plans drone coverage; reviewed imagery supports Field Supervisor/planning; suspend unsafe flights; retain physical inspections. Crew Transfer Vessel/Daughter Craft/Service Operations Vessel/Helideck support transport; North Access Scanner/South Access Scanner/Personnel Tracking Console track accountability. Warehouse System/Storekeeper/Spares Hub/Port Agent manage supplies/logistics; Warehouse System produces Backorder Exception Slip. Portal retains requests/revisions/reviews/start/pause/resumption/completion/auditable closure. Requests specify location/scope/duration/team/equipment; reviewers assess hazards/controls/access/coordination, HSE Officer risks, technical reviewers compatibility. Return incompleteness; authorize only recorded reviews/controls, bounded scope/location/time/personnel. Field Supervisor verifies

New part:
S173: During normal operation, station service transformers at the Offshore Substation supply the facility's auxiliary electrical loads from the medium-voltage collection system.
S174: The normal supply serves control systems, lighting, ventilation, communications, and equipment required for safe switching and maintenance.
S175: Essential loads are separated from nonessential loads so that backup capacity can be reserved for safety and control functions.
S176: The Emergency Generator is assigned the operational alias Foxglove for maintenance and alarm references.
S177: On loss of the normal auxiliary supply, automatic controls initiate the Emergency Generator start sequence.
S178: Transfer to the emergency bus occurs only after voltage and frequency are within the configured acceptance limits.
S179: The transfer arrangement prevents the normal and emergency sources from being connected in parallel unless an approved synchronizing function is provided.
S180: The Emergency Generator supplies the designated emergency distribution bus and is not intended to support turbine export production.
S181: Loads connected to the emergency distribution bus are prioritized according to their contribution to personnel safety, equipment protection, and controlled shutdown.
S182: Nonessential loads are shed automatically when generator capacity is insufficient or the measured load exceeds its operating limit.
S183: If the Emergency Generator does not start or stabilize, the system raises an alarm and maintains any available uninterruptible control power.
S184: Operators use the approved recovery procedure to assess the fault, preserve essential services, and restore the normal supply when it is safe to do so.
S185: The Electrical Technician verifies protective device settings and transfer interlocks during planned maintenance.
S186: Scheduled exercising confirms that the Emergency Generator can start, accept its expected load, and operate for the required test duration.
S187: Fuel condition, cooling, lubrication, battery readiness, and exhaust ventilation are checked as part of the generator readiness program.
S188: Maintenance Planning Engine schedules inspections and corrective work using equipment condition and operating history.
S189: Morrowick maintains the designated emergency distribution bus within its approved operating limits.
S190: The Grid Interface Relay provides status indications that support assessment of the normal supply and its protective state.
S191: The Turbine Controller enters its configured safe operating mode when required auxiliary services are unavailable.
S192: The SCADA Gateway presents supply alarms and generator status to the Shore Control Room for remote awareness.
S193: The Control Engineer reviews persistent alarms and coordinates electrical support with the Substation Operator.
S194: Metocean Buoy produces the Wave Burst Record at the configured sampling interval.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
